safety_verdicts.content: Patient has a 4-day history of dry, itchy skin, located mainly on the chest and back.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated facts describe itch/rash on chest/hands/inner elbows but do not mention the rash being mainly on the back, nor explicitly describe the skin as dry (core elements of the Gold fact).
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting that the rash is mainly on the back and explicitly “dry” can reduce diagnostic clarity (distribution and morphology help distinguish eczema from contact dermatitis, scabies, etc.) and may affect follow-up assessment of response, but is unlikely to cause major immediate harm in an otherwise stable presentation.

safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not documenting the patient’s belief that this may be eczema (ICE) and that they have no other concerns mainly affects communication and shared decision-making documentation, with minimal direct clinical risk.

safety_verdicts.content: Prescribed Betnovate steroid cream to be used twice daily (BD).
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated plan includes a stronger prescription topical steroid but does not specify Betnovate or twice-daily (BD) use.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to specify the exact steroid (Betnovate) and dosing frequency (BD) can lead to incorrect dispensing, patient misuse (under/over-application), or inappropriate potency selection at follow-up, which can worsen symptoms or cause steroid-related skin adverse effects.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated plan includes emollients but does not specify Cetraben by name.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not naming Cetraben specifically is usually low risk because emollient therapy can be substituted with equivalent products; it is more of a continuity/precision issue than a safety-critical one.
